title: Impact experiments ledger — Zoe Hart
content:
Context: quick scratchpad for running small, measurable experiments that nudge my quarter impact. Treat like a lightweight lab notebook — short hypothesis -> metric -> low-effort run -> signal -> next step. Will bring highlights to 1:1s and mid-quarter calibration.

Guiding constraints (personal):
- Timebox each experiment to <= 2 weeks of active work.
- Aim for experiments that (a) produce a measurable signal and (b) are reusable as artifacts (template/email/code snippet, mini-runbook).
- Prioritize things that reduce friction for teammates or surface measurable org-level outcomes.

Experiment 1 — Async onboarding digest
- Hypothesis: A concise 5-min weekly digest for new hires reduces first-30-day ad-hoc questions by 20%.
- Metric(s): # ad-hoc onboarding questions per new hire (Slack threads + calendar invites) in first 30 days; baseline (last cohort): ~12 questions/hire.
- Experiment: Draft 6 short digest items (how-to links, common gotchas, who to ping). Send to next cohort weekly for first 3 weeks.
- Timebox: 10 hours to draft + 3 weeks sending/observing.
- Signal threshold: 20% reduction vs baseline or clear qualitative feedback.
- Notes: pair with solutions-eng for a 'what-I-wish-I-knew' line. If positive, convert to template and add to hiring checklist.

Experiment 2 — Micro-feedback sprints
- Hypothesis: Running a 2-week micro-feedback sprint (ask 5 peers for 1-sentence feedback each) increases perceived clarity score on my team survey by +0.3 points.
- Metric(s): Perceived clarity (pulse survey) pre/post; response rate to feedback request.
- Experiment: Identify 5 recent collaborators, send structured prompt with examples, collect, reflect, summarize for manager.
- Timebox: 4 hours framing + 1 hour consolidation.
- Risk: low. Data quality depends on ask framing.

Experiment 3 — Meeting agenda template A/B
- Hypothesis: Explicit 3-line pre-reads reduce meeting overrun and increase decisions made.
- Metric(s): % meetings ending on time, # decisions captured in notes.
- Experiment: For next 6 recurring meetings I run, alternate between current approach and the 3-line pre-read; track outcomes in a shared tracker.
- Timebox: 2 hours setup + tracking for 6 meetings.

Signals I care about (priority order):
1) Downstream time saved for at least two teammates (qualitative + 1 measurable case). 
2) Fewer follow-up clarifying questions after docs or meetings. 
3) Reuse of artifact by >1 other person.

Manager sync: talking points for next 1:1
- Quick 30s summary of experiments + one early-lead signal.
- Ask for 1 intro to a partner (x-team) to scale the onboarding digest if it shows signal.
- Calibration check: are these aligned to my quarter priorities (focus on reducing operational friction)?
- Raise any blockers (access to cohort list for metric tracking).

Data capture plan (minimal):
- Use a single ledger sheet (sprint column, date started, metric baseline, metric after, qualitative notes). For now I'll keep it in this doc; if it hits signal migrate to shared sheet and link.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a quick way to capture ad-hoc onboarding question counts (manual tally vs ask new hires a single micro-survey).
- Draft a 3-sentence template for feedback request and test phrasing (high specificity vs open ask).
- Decide whether a successful experiment becomes part of my personal checklist or a team standard (flag for manager).

Reflection notes (ongoing)
- I tend to underestimate conversation friction; the real win is often the latent time reclaimed by others rather than direct headcount time.
- Keep experiments small and defensible; don't over-index on broad organizational change without partner support.

Next immediate actions (this week)
- Draft onboarding digest (first 6 items) and send to Maya for quick review (2/3 days).
- Finalize feedback request template and send to 2 peers for pilot.
- Add a simple tracker table beneath this doc and populate baseline counts for last cohort.
